docs.title: openai-usage
docs.text:
One usage model for every OpenAI API.

openai-usage collapses the dozen different Usage shapes scattered across the OpenAI Python SDK into a single, additive Usage object — then estimates what it costs against live model pricing.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The OpenAI SDK reports usage in a different shape for almost every endpoint: Chat Completions, the Responses API, the Agents SDK, Realtime, Batch, Embeddings, Images, and Transcription each have their own Usage type with their own field names. Aggregating spend across them means writing the same adapter code again and again.

This library does that adapting once. You hand it whatever the SDK gave you, and you get back a uniform Usage you can add up and price.

from openai_usage import Usage

total = Usage()
total.add(Usage.from_openai(chat_completion.usage))      # Chat Completions
total.add(Usage.from_openai(response.usage))             # Responses API
total.add(Usage.from_openai(realtime_event.response.usage))  # Realtime

print(total.input_tokens, total.output_tokens, total.total_tokens)
print(f"${total.estimate_cost('gpt-4o'):.6f}")

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Unify every usage type

    A single Usage.from_openai(...) accepts Chat Completions, Responses, Agents SDK, Realtime, Batch, Embeddings, Images, Transcription, and Assistants runs.

  • Add it all up

    Usage.add() accumulates requests, tokens, and per-modality token details across calls — including cached, cache-write, reasoning, audio, image, video, and text tokens.

  • Estimate cost

    Price usage against any model using live LiteLLM and OpenRouter pricing, with separate rates for cached, cache-write, reasoning, audio, image, and duration.

  • Pydantic-native

    Usage is a pydantic.BaseModel — serialize it, store it, and validate it anywhere, with full backward compatibility for older payloads.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: A concise tour of the public surface. Everything below is importable from openai_usage unless noted otherwise.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: The core model. See Tracking Usage for the field table.

docs.title: Usage.from_openai(openai_usage, *, inplace=False) -> Usage
docs.text:
Build a normalized Usage (with requests=1) from any supported usage type. This is the only entry point — it accepts the OpenAI SDK types plus google-genai and litellm usage.

  • openai_usage — any object in the AnyUsage union.
  • inplace — when True, return the constructed instance directly; when False (default), return a re-validated copy.
  • Raises ValueError for an unsupported type.

docs.title: Usage.add(other) -> None
docs.text: Accumulate other into self, in place. Sums requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, seconds, and every field of both token-detail breakdowns (cached, cache-write, reasoning, audio, image, text, video).

docs.title: Usage.estimate_cost(model=None, *, realtime_pricing=False, ignore_not_found=True) -> float
docs.text:
Estimate the cost of this usage as a float. See Estimating Costs.

  • model — a resolved model object, a model-name str, or None to fall back to Usage.model (then to gpt-4o-mini).
  • realtime_pricing — ignore the cache TTL and re-download both catalogs.
  • ignore_not_found — return 0.0 for an unknown model (default) instead of raising ValueError.

docs.title: Usage.estimate_cost_str(...) -> str
docs.text: Same parameters as estimate_cost, but returns the exact Decimal cost as a string with no float rounding.

docs.title: UsageInputTokensDetails
docs.text:
Extends openai.types.responses.InputTokensDetails.

Field Default Source cached_tokens — OpenAI schema cache_write_tokens 0 OpenAI schema audio_tokens 0 extension text_tokens 0 extension image_tokens 0 extension video_tokens 0 extension

cache_write_tokens mirrors the field newer OpenAI SDKs add to InputTokensDetails. It is redefined with a 0 default so the model stays constructible on both older SDKs (which lack the field) and newer ones (which make it required).

docs.title: UsageOutputTokensDetails
docs.text:
Extends openai.types.responses.OutputTokensDetails.

Field Default Source reasoning_tokens — OpenAI schema audio_tokens 0 extension text_tokens 0 extension image_tokens 0 extension video_tokens 0 extension

docs.title: AnyUsage
docs.text:
A typing.Union of every usage type accepted by from_openai, including the optional google-genai and litellm types. Use it to type your own functions:

from openai_usage import AnyUsage, Usage

def track(raw: AnyUsage) -> Usage:
    return Usage.from_openai(raw)

docs.title: OpenAIUsage
docs.text: The OpenAI-only subset of AnyUsage, kept for backward compatibility.

docs.title: get_model(model_name, *, realtime_pricing=False) -> PricedModel | None
docs.text:
Resolve a model name across both catalogs. Returns None when nothing matches.

from openai_usage.pricing import get_model

model = get_model("gpt-4o")
print(model.pricing.price_per_input_token_without_cached)
print(model.pricing.price_per_output_audio_token)

docs.title: ModelPricing
docs.text:
A runtime-checkable Protocol describing the rates the estimator needs, so both catalogs can be priced through one interface:

price_per_request, price_per_input_token_without_cached, price_per_input_token_with_cached, price_per_input_cache_write_token, price_per_output_not_reasoning_token, price_per_output_reasoning_token, price_per_input_audio_token, price_per_output_audio_token, price_per_input_image_token, price_per_output_image_token, price_per_second.

Every property returns a decimal.Decimal, and is 0 when the catalog has no figure for it.

docs.title: PricedModel
docs.text: A runtime-checkable Protocol with id: str and pricing: ModelPricing. OpenRouterModel and LiteLLMModel both satisfy it.

docs.title: Cache controls
docs.text: openai_usage.pricing.cache_dir(), ttl_seconds() and is_offline() report the effective cache settings. See Estimating Costs for the environment variables.

docs.title: openai_usage.pricing.litellm
docs.text:
Function Returns get_model(name) One LiteLLMModel, exact key first then relaxed get_model_exact(name) Exact catalog key only, case-insensitive get_model_loose(name) Relaxed matching only get_entries() The raw catalog entries as dict[str, dict] get_models() The whole catalog, validated

The catalog is held as raw entries and validated one model at a time, so a lookup builds only what it returns. get_models() validates all ~3,000 of them, so prefer get_model() unless you genuinely want the full set.

All of these return empty or None rather than raising when the source is unreachable — there is no bundled snapshot for this catalog.

docs.title: openai_usage.pricing.open_router
docs.text:
get_models(realtime_pricing=False), get_model(name), plus OpenRouterModel, OpenRouterPricing and the rest of the catalog schema.

OpenRouterPricing keeps its original price_per_audio_token and price_per_image_token properties alongside the split input/output ones.

Name matching is exposed too, since both catalogs share it:

Function Purpose matches_loosely(name, model_id) One-shot relaxed match normalize_query(name) Precompute the three forms a name is matched under matches_normalized(query, model_id) Match an already-normalized query

Use the latter two when scanning many ids; matches_loosely re-derives the normalized forms on every call.

openai_usage.extra.open_router is deprecated

It still re-exports everything it did in v0.9.x, so existing imports keep working. New code should import from openai_usage.pricing.open_router.

docs.title: Estimating Costs
docs.text:
Once you have a Usage object, you can estimate what it cost against any model's pricing.

from openai_usage import Usage

usage = Usage(requests=1, input_tokens=1000, output_tokens=2000, total_tokens=3000)

cost = usage.estimate_cost("gpt-4o")
print(f"${cost:.6f}")

docs.title: Two return types
docs.text:
Method Returns Use when estimate_cost(...) float You want a number to display or compare. estimate_cost_str(...) str You need exact decimal precision (it returns the raw Decimal as a string, with no float rounding). 
usage.estimate_cost("gpt-4o")        # 0.0225
usage.estimate_cost_str("gpt-4o")    # "0.0225"

docs.title: Choosing the model
docs.text:
The model can come from three places, in order of precedence:

  1. The argument: usage.estimate_cost("anthropic/claude-3-haiku").
  2. The Usage.model field, if the argument is omitted.
  3. A gpt-4o-mini fallback if neither is set (a warning is logged).
usage.model = "gpt-4o"
usage.estimate_cost()          # uses usage.model

usage.estimate_cost("o1")      # argument wins over usage.model

docs.title: Pricing data
docs.text:
Pricing comes from two catalogs, both fetched at runtime:

Source Covers LiteLLM ~3,000 models across every provider, including the embedding, image, audio and transcription models OpenRouter never proxies OpenRouter The chat models OpenRouter proxies, under vendor/model names

A name is resolved in three steps:

  1. LiteLLM exact key. LiteLLM files models under their native ids (gpt-4o, whisper-1, claude-sonnet-4-5), so most names hit here immediately.
  2. OpenRouter relaxed matching. Handles vendor/model names, aliases, and separator differences (claude-haiku-4-5 finds anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5).
  3. LiteLLM relaxed matching, as a last resort.

You can also pass a fully resolved model object instead of a name.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
Both catalogs are cached on disk so the download happens at most once a day.

Setting Default Environment variable Cache directory ./.cache/openai-usage/ OPENAI_USAGE_CACHE_DIR Time to live 86400 (one day) OPENAI_USAGE_CACHE_TTL Disable network off OPENAI_USAGE_OFFLINE

Passing realtime_pricing=True ignores the TTL and re-downloads both catalogs:

usage.estimate_cost("anthropic/claude-3-haiku", realtime_pricing=True)

docs.title: When the network is unavailable
docs.text:
Nothing raises. Each step falls through to the next:

fresh cache -> network fetch -> stale cache -> bundled snapshot

The bundled snapshot is an OpenRouter catalog shipped inside the package, so pricing keeps working offline for the models it covers. LiteLLM has no bundled snapshot; without a cache entry its lookups return nothing and resolution falls back to OpenRouter.

Set OPENAI_USAGE_OFFLINE=1 to skip the network entirely — useful in airgapped environments and in tests. Connect and read timeouts are deliberately short, so an unreachable network fails fast instead of stalling a caller the bundled snapshot could have served.

A catalog that had to degrade — a failed fetch, or a fall back to the bundled snapshot — is only held in memory for a minute rather than the full day, so a process that started while the network was down picks up the real catalog once it recovers.

docs.title: Cost of the first lookup
docs.text: Catalog entries are validated one at a time, as they are looked up, rather than all at once. A first lookup with a warm cache costs a few milliseconds and holds only the models it actually returned; the ~3,000-entry LiteLLM catalog is never fully materialized unless you ask for it with get_models().

docs.title: How the estimate is computed
docs.text:
Tokens are split into disjoint buckets and each is priced at its own rate:

Bucket Rate Cached input tokens cache-read price Cache-write input tokens cache-creation price Audio input tokens input audio price Audio output tokens output audio price Image input tokens input image price Image output tokens output image price Reasoning output tokens reasoning price, falling back to the completion price Remaining input tokens prompt price Remaining output tokens completion price Requests per-request price Seconds per-second price

When a usage object carries no audio, image, cached, or reasoning detail — an ordinary chat completion, say — every special bucket is 0 and the math reduces to the familiar prompt × input + completion × output.

docs.title: Unknown models
docs.text:
By default, an unrecognized model name yields a 0.0 cost and a logged warning, so a bad id never crashes an aggregation pipeline:

usage.estimate_cost("not-a-real-model")          # 0.0 (warns)

Set ignore_not_found=False to raise instead:

usage.estimate_cost("not-a-real-model", ignore_not_found=False)  # raises ValueError

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Video tokens are billed as text

video_tokens are recorded for reporting, but neither catalog publishes a per-token video rate, so they stay in the plain-text remainder and are billed at the ordinary input rate. That matches how the providers reporting them bill today, but verify it if video is a large share of your spend.

Detail buckets are assumed disjoint

Cached, cache-write, audio and image counts are subtracted from the totals to derive the plain-text remainder. If a provider reports overlapping buckets — a cached audio token counted in both — that token is subtracted twice and the estimate comes out low.

OpenRouter publishes one rate per modality

OpenRouter has a single audio and a single image rate per model, so a model resolved through OpenRouter uses that one rate for both input and output. LiteLLM prices them separately and is tried first, so this normally only applies to models LiteLLM does not carry.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
openai-usage requires Python 3.11+.

pippoetryuv 
pip install openai-usage

poetry add openai-usage

uv add openai-usage

The openai and openai-agents SDKs are installed as dependencies, so the usage types you pass to Usage.from_openai are available out of the box.

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Install an extra only if you want to hand Usage.from_openai that SDK's usage object. Neither is imported unless you already imported it yourself, so skipping them costs you nothing.

pippoetryuv 
pip install "openai-usage[google-genai]"
pip install "openai-usage[litellm]"
pip install "openai-usage[all]"

poetry add "openai-usage[all]"

uv add "openai-usage[all]"
Extra Adds support for google-genai GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata (Gemini) litellm litellm.types.utils.Usage all Both

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
import openai_usage

print(openai_usage.__version__)

docs.title: What gets installed
docs.text:
Dependency Purpose openai Source of the SDK usage types (CompletionUsage, ResponseUsage, …). openai-agents Agents SDK usage (agents.Usage, agents.RunContextWrapper). pydantic Usage is a Pydantic model. requests Fetching the pricing catalogs.

Model pricing is fetched at runtime from LiteLLM and OpenRouter, then cached under ./.cache/openai-usage/ for a day. A bundled snapshot keeps things working offline. See Estimating Costs.

docs.title: Supported Usage Types
docs.text:
Usage.from_openai() accepts every usage object below. Each is normalized into the same Usage shape with requests=1.

OpenAI source Type passed to from_openai What is captured Chat Completions openai.types.completion_usage.CompletionUsage input/output tokens, cached, reasoning Responses API openai.types.responses.ResponseUsage input/output tokens, cached, reasoning Agents SDK agents.Usage input/output tokens, cached, reasoning Agents SDK (context) agents.RunContextWrapper unwrapped to its .usage Realtime openai.types.realtime.RealtimeResponseUsage input/output tokens, cached, audio, text Batch openai.types.batch_usage.BatchUsage input/output tokens, cached, reasoning Embeddings openai.types.create_embedding_response.Usage input tokens only (no output) Images (gpt-image-1) openai.types.images_response.Usage input/output tokens, image, text Transcription (tokens) openai.types.audio.transcription.UsageTokens input/output tokens, audio, text Transcription (duration) openai.types.audio.transcription.UsageDuration seconds only Assistants run openai.types.beta.threads.run.Usage prompt/completion tokens Assistants run step openai.types.beta.threads.runs.run_step.Usage prompt/completion tokens

docs.title: Other providers
docs.text:
Two non-OpenAI SDKs are supported through the same from_openai() call, each behind an optional extra:

Source Type passed to from_openai What is captured Gemini google.genai.types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata input/output tokens, cached, thinking, tool-use prompt, per-modality audio/image/video/text LiteLLM litellm.types.utils.Usage input/output tokens, cached, cache-write, reasoning, audio/image/video/text, cost

Neither SDK is imported unless you already imported it yourself, so installing the extras is only necessary if you actually pass their objects.

# Gemini
response = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-2.5-pro", contents="hi")
usage = Usage.from_openai(response.usage_metadata)

# LiteLLM
response = litellm.completion(model="claude-sonnet-4-5", messages=messages)
usage = Usage.from_openai(response.usage)

Two mapping decisions are worth knowing about:

  • Gemini reports thoughts_token_count separately from candidates_token_count. output_tokens is the sum of both, and reasoning_tokens holds the thinking count.
  • Gemini's tool_use_prompt_token_count is added to input_tokens, since it is billed as input.

All the OpenAI types are also re-exported from the package root for convenience and type hints:

from openai_usage import (
    BatchUsage,
    EmbeddingUsage,
    ImagesUsage,
    RealtimeResponseUsage,
    RunStepUsage,
    RunUsage,
    TranscriptionUsageDuration,
    TranscriptionUsageTokens,
    AnyUsage,     # the Union of everything from_openai accepts
    OpenAIUsage,  # the OpenAI-only subset
)

docs.title: Realtime (audio)
docs.text:
from openai_usage import Usage

# event is a `response.done` event from a realtime session
usage = Usage.from_openai(event.response.usage)

print(usage.input_tokens_details.audio_tokens)
print(usage.output_tokens_details.audio_tokens)

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
response = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input="hello")
usage = Usage.from_openai(response.usage)

assert usage.output_tokens == 0   # embeddings have no generated output

docs.title: Image generation
docs.text:
result = client.images.generate(model="gpt-image-1", prompt="a red bicycle")
usage = Usage.from_openai(result.usage)

print(usage.input_tokens_details.image_tokens)
print(usage.output_tokens_details.image_tokens)

docs.title: Transcription
docs.text:
from openai_usage import Usage

# gpt-4o-transcribe → billed by tokens
usage = Usage.from_openai(transcription.usage)        # UsageTokens
print(usage.input_tokens_details.audio_tokens)

# whisper-1 → billed by duration
usage = Usage.from_openai(transcription.usage)        # UsageDuration
print(usage.seconds)

Not LLM usage? Not included.

OpenAI's organization-level Usage API (/organization/usage/*) reports aggregated billing buckets rather than per-call token counts, so it is intentionally out of scope for this library.

docs.title: Tracking Usage
docs.text: The Usage model is the heart of the library. It holds the token counts for one or many API calls and knows how to build itself from any OpenAI usage object.

docs.title: The Usage model
docs.text:
from openai_usage import Usage

usage = Usage(
    requests=1,
    input_tokens=100,
    output_tokens=200,
    total_tokens=300,
)
Field Type Description requests int Number of billable calls represented. input_tokens int Total input (prompt) tokens. input_tokens_details UsageInputTokensDetails Breakdown: cached, cache_write, audio, image, video, text. output_tokens int Total output (completion) tokens. output_tokens_details UsageOutputTokensDetails Breakdown: reasoning, audio, image, video, text. total_tokens int Input + output tokens. seconds float Audio duration for duration-billed transcription. model str \| None Optional model id, used as the default for cost estimation. cost str \| float \| None Optional slot to stash an estimated cost.

The two detail models extend OpenAI's own schema, so the familiar fields keep working while the new per-modality counts default to 0:

usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens   # from the OpenAI schema
usage.input_tokens_details.audio_tokens    # extension, defaults to 0
usage.input_tokens_details.image_tokens    # extension, defaults to 0
usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens

docs.title: Building from OpenAI objects
docs.text:
Usage.from_openai() accepts any supported SDK usage object and returns a normalized Usage with requests=1. See Supported Usage Types for the full list.

from openai import OpenAI
from openai_usage import Usage

client = OpenAI()

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)

usage = Usage.from_openai(completion.usage)
print(usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens)

It works the same way across APIs — the call below is identical in spirit for the Responses API, the Agents SDK, Realtime, Batch, Embeddings, Images, and Transcription:

# Responses API
usage = Usage.from_openai(response.usage)

# Agents SDK — pass the Usage or the RunContextWrapper
usage = Usage.from_openai(result.context_wrapper)

# Realtime — from a response.done event
usage = Usage.from_openai(event.response.usage)

inplace for hot loops

By default from_openai returns a fresh, fully re-validated instance. When you are aggregating large volumes and trust the input, pass inplace=True to skip the extra serialization round-trip.

usage = Usage.from_openai(completion.usage, inplace=True)

docs.title: Combining usage
docs.text:
Usage.add() accumulates another Usage into the current one — requests, tokens, every token-detail breakdown, and seconds. This is how you roll up the spend of an entire agent run, a batch job, or a whole day of traffic.

from openai_usage import Usage

total = Usage()
for completion in completions:
    total.add(Usage.from_openai(completion.usage))

print(f"Requests:      {total.requests}")
print(f"Input tokens:  {total.input_tokens}")
print(f"Output tokens: {total.output_tokens}")
print(f"Cached tokens: {total.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens}")
print(f"Audio tokens:  {total.input_tokens_details.audio_tokens}")

add mutates in place

add modifies the receiver and returns None. Start from a fresh Usage() accumulator rather than mutating a value you still need.

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text:
Usage is a plain Pydantic model, so it serializes and restores cleanly:

blob = usage.model_dump_json()
restored = Usage.model_validate_json(blob)

Payloads serialized by older versions of the library — before the audio, image, video, and duration fields existed — still validate. The new fields simply default to 0, so stored history keeps working after an upgrade.
